residencyRequirements.description: At least one party must have been an actual bona fide resident of West Virginia for one year. However, if the parties were married in West Virginia and one party still resides there, no minimum residency duration is required. (W. Va. Code §48-5-105)

waitingPeriod.description: West Virginia has no mandatory post-filing waiting period. However, for no-fault divorce based on irreconcilable differences, either both parties must consent or the parties must have lived separate and apart for one year prior to filing. (W. Va. Code §48-5-201 et seq.)

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Differences
noFault.description: Irreconcilable differences exist between the parties (requires consent of both parties or one-year separation)

noFault.name: Voluntary Separation (1 Year)
noFault.description: The parties have lived separate and apart without cohabitation for one year

fault.name: Felony Conviction
fault.description: Conviction of a felony or infamous offense after the marriage

fault.name: Cruel or Inhuman Treatment
fault.description: Cruel or inhuman treatment, including false accusations of adultery

fault.name: Habitual Drunkenness or Drug Addiction
fault.description: Habitual drunkenness or habitual addiction to drugs

fault.name: Abuse or Neglect of a Child
fault.description: Abuse or neglect of a child of the parties

groundsForDissolution.notes: West Virginia allows both fault and no-fault divorce. For no-fault based on irreconcilable differences, both parties must consent, or the parties must have been separated for one year.

propertyDivision.description: West Virginia is an equitable distribution state. The court divides marital property equitably, considering the length of the marriage, contributions of each spouse (including homemaking), the income and earning capacity of each party, and other relevant factors.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Separate property includes property acquired before the marriage and property acquired by gift or inheritance. Separate property is generally not subject to division unless it was commingled with marital property.

legalCitations.description: Residency requirement — 1 year (or no minimum if married in WV)
Grounds for divorce — fault and no-fault
Child custody — allocation of custodial responsibility
West Virginia Child Support Guidelines — income shares model

filingFees.notes: West Virginia charges a standard $135 filing fee for a Petition for Divorce in Family Court per W. Va. Code §59-1-11. Modifications of Family Court orders cost $85 and miscellaneous Family Court petitions cost $200. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals via Financial Affidavit Form SCA-C&M201.

basic.name: Answer or Waiver
basic.description: Respondent's response or waiver of service

basic.name: Financial Statement
basic.description: Disclosure of income, assets, and debts

basic.name: Final Divorce Order
basic.description: Final court order granting the divorce

service.name: Personal Service
service.description: Service by sheriff or process server

service.name: Acceptance of Service
service.notes: Must be signed by respondent and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Required plan detailing allocation of custodial responsibility and parenting time

withChildren.name: Child Support Calculation Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per West Virginia Child Support Guidelines (W. Va. Code §48-13-101)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per West Virginia court filing requirements

inState.description: Respondent must file a response within 20 days of service

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside West Virginia must file a response within 30 days of service

childSupportGuidelines.description: West Virginia uses an income shares model. Both parents' adjusted gross incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined monthly income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust or inappropriate. Shared custody adjustments may apply.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: West Virginia courts may award spousal support based on the needs of the requesting spouse and the ability of the other spouse to pay, considering the length of the marriage, the standard of living during the marriage, the age and health of the parties, the income and earning capacity of each spouse, the education and training of each party, and other relevant factors.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Either party may request spousal support. The court has broad discretion in determining the amount and duration.

court.name: Family Court
court.description: Divorce cases are filed in the Family Court of the county where either party resides. (W. Va. Code §51-2A)
